items.title: The radial composite $x\mapsto u(\lvert x\rvert)$ on an annulus: $C^k$ regularity and $\nabla\bigl(u\circ\lvert\cdot\rvert\bigr)(x)=u'(\lvert x\rvert)\,x/\lvert x\rvert$
items.statement:
Let $J_0\subseteq(0,\infty)$ be an open interval
([[def-interval]]), let $u:J_0\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^k$ for some
$k\ge1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and put
$$A:=\{\,x\in\mathbb R^3:\lvert x\rvert\in J_0\,\},\qquad \lvert x\rvert:=\lVert x\rVert_2=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle},$$
the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Then:

1. $A$ is open in $\mathbb R^3$ and $0\notin A$;
2. the function $N:A\to(0,\infty)$, $N(x):=\lvert x\rvert$, is of class
   $C^\infty$ on $A$; it is totally differentiable at every $x\in A$
   ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]) with
   $$DN(x)h=\frac{\langle x,h\rangle}{\lvert x\rvert}\qquad(h\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad\text{so}\qquad\nabla N(x)=\frac{x}{\lvert x\rvert}$$
   ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]);
3. the radial composite $U:=u\circ N:A\to\mathbb R$, $U(x)=u(\lvert x\rvert)$,
   is of class $C^k$ on $A$ and totally differentiable at every $x\in A$
   with
   $$DU(x)h=u'(\lvert x\rvert)\,\frac{\langle x,h\rangle}{\lvert x\rvert}=\Bigl\langle u'(\lvert x\rvert)\frac{x}{\lvert x\rvert},\,h\Bigr\rangle\qquad(h\in\mathbb R^3),$$
   that is, $\nabla U(x)=u'(\lvert x\rvert)\,x/\lvert x\rvert$.
items.strategy: A direct proof: compute the difference quotient of the norm, identify the total derivative, obtain the gradient of the radial composite by the chain rule, and run an induction on smoothness.

items.title: Two-body reduction of a static central pair-potential model: the relative coordinate is a central-force trajectory for the reduced mass, the centre of mass moves uniformly, and the reconstruction is a bijection
items.statement:
Adopt the force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=2$
labels, masses $m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time
window $I_0$, and the collision-excluded configuration domain
$$Q:=\{\,x=(x_1,x_2)\in(\mathbb R^3)^2:\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert\in J_0\,\}$$
for an open interval $J_0\subseteq(0,\infty)$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]). Suppose the model presents its force map
through the time-independent potential
$$U(x_1,x_2):=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert),$$
where $u:J_0\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^2$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so that
$F_i(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_i}U(x)$ on the state domain ([[post-cm02-interactions]],
clauses (iii) and (iv), [[lem-cm05-radial-potential-gradient]]). Let
$x:J\to Q$ be a **motion** of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty
interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) and write
$$M:=m_1+m_2,\quad \mu:=\frac{m_1m_2}{M},\quad X:=\frac{m_1x_1+m_2x_2}{M},\quad V:=X',\quad P:=m_1x_1'+m_2x_2',\quad r:=x_1-x_2,$$
with $\lvert\cdot\rvert=\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ the Euclidean norm
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) and dimensions as in [[def-cm01-units]]
($[M]=[\mu]=\mu$, $[X]=[r]=\ell$, $[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$). Then:

1. **(Pair forces.)** On $J$ the evaluated forces are
   $$F_1\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=-\frac{u'(\lvert r\rvert)}{\lvert r\rvert}\,r,\qquad F_2\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=+\frac{u'(\lvert r\rvert)}{\lvert r\rvert}\,r;$$
   thus the model invokes the external-plus-pair presentation of
   [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (i) with
   $F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$ and the single pair force
   $F_{12}=-u'(\lvert r\rvert)r/\lvert r\rvert=-F_{21}$, which is central
   and antisymmetric in the sense of clause (ii).
2. **(Centre of mass.)** $P$ is constant on $J$ and $X$ is affine: for all
   $t,t_0\in J$, $X(t)=X(t_0)+(t-t_0)V$ with the constant
   $V=X'=M^{-1}P$.
3. **(Relative motion.)** $r$ is of class $C^2$ on $J$, satisfies
   $$\mu\,r''(t)=-\frac{u'(\lvert r(t)\rvert)}{\lvert r(t)\rvert}\,r(t)\qquad(t\in J),$$
   and is therefore a **central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$** in the
   sense of [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]]; its angular momentum vector
   $j=\mu\,r\times r'$ and energy $E=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+
   u(\lvert r\rvert)$ are the attached objects of that definition.
4. **(Reconstruction and bijection.)** The identities
   $x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$ and $x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$ hold on $J$.
   Conversely, if $X^{\circ}:J\to\mathbb R^3$ is affine with
   $(X^{\circ})''=0$ and $r^{\circ}:J\to\mathbb R^3$ is a $C^2$ curve with
   $\lvert r^{\circ}(t)\rvert\in J_0$ and
   $\mu(r^{\circ})''=-u'(\lvert r^{\circ}\rvert)r^{\circ}/\lvert r^{\circ}\rvert$
   on $J$, then
   $$x_1^{\circ}:=X^{\circ}+\frac{m_2}{M}r^{\circ},\qquad x_2^{\circ}:=X^{\circ}-\frac{m_1}{M}r^{\circ}$$
   define a motion $x^{\circ}:J\to Q$ of the model whose centre of mass is
   $X^{\circ}$ and whose relative coordinate is $r^{\circ}$. Consequently
   the assignment $x\mapsto(X,r)$ is a bijection from the motions of the
   model on $J$ onto the pairs (affine curve $X^{\circ}$ with
   $(X^{\circ})''=0$\!, central-force trajectory $r^{\circ}$ for $(\mu,u)$
   with values in $J_0$) on $J$.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: evaluate the pair potential's gradients to obtain the central antisymmetric pair forces, apply the momentum balance with vanishing external force, divide the two equations of motion by the masses to get the reduced central-force equation, and reconstruct the motion from the centre-of-mass and relative data.
items.physical_scope: The conditional reduction of a two-label model whose force map is presented by a static central pair potential: along every motion the evaluated pair forces are central and antisymmetric, the total momentum and the centre-of-mass velocity are constant, the relative coordinate satisfies the one-body central-force equation with the reduced mass, and the motion is reconstructed from the centre-of-mass motion and the relative trajectory. The result is a deduction inside the adopted force and interaction branches; it uses no measured value, assumes no external forces, excludes collisions, and asserts no conservation law beyond the vanishing of the total external force that the presentation supplies.

items.title: Adopted central-force model class: static central pair potentials, the reduced one-label problem, the fixed-centre idealization, reading conventions and exclusions
items.statement:
Adopt, as the **central-force model** for the two-body part of this page, the
following restricted model class inside the force and interaction branches of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]].

**(i) The two-label central model.** A model of class (i) is a force model of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=2$ labels, fixed masses
$m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time window $I_0$, the
collision-excluded configuration domain
$$Q:=\{\,x=(x_1,x_2)\in(\mathbb R^3)^2:\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert\in J_0\,\}$$
for an open interval $J_0\subseteq(0,\infty)$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), and the force map presented through the
time-independent **static central pair potential**
$$U(x_1,x_2):=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert),\qquad u:J_0\to\mathbb R\ \text{of class }C^2,$$
so that $F_i(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_i}U(x)$ on the state domain (clauses (iii)
and (iv) of [[post-cm02-interactions]]; $U$ is of class $C^2$ on the open
$Q$ by [[lem-cm05-radial-potential-gradient]]). In the external-plus-pair
presentation of clause (i) of that postulate the model has
$F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$: no external forces act on the labels of a model
of class (i).

**(ii) The reduced one-label problem.** For a model of class (i) put
$\mu:=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)>0$ of dimension $\mu$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). The
**reduced problem** of the model is the one-label problem of mass $\mu$ whose
unknown is the relative coordinate $r=x_1-x_2$ and whose equation is
$$\mu\,r''=-\frac{u'(\lvert r\rvert)}{\lvert r\rvert}\,r;$$
by [[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] the relative coordinate of every motion
of a model of class (i) solves this equation, and every pair of a uniform
centre-of-mass motion and a solution of the reduced equation on a common
interval reconstructs a motion of the model. Adopt the reduced problem as the
object that the central-force statements of this page describe, and the
central-force-trajectory vocabulary of
[[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] (attached angular momentum
$j=\mu\,r\times r'$ and energy $E=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+u(\lvert
r\rvert)$) as the vocabulary in which those statements are phrased.

**(iii) The one-label fixed-centre idealization.** A **one-label central
model** is a force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$,
mass $\mu>0$, time window $I_0$, a fixed **centre** $c\in\mathbb R^3$, the
configuration domain $Q_c=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lvert x-c\rvert\in J_0\}$, and
the external force map
$$F(t,x,v)=-\frac{u'(\lvert x-c\rvert)}{\lvert x-c\rvert}\,(x-c),$$
presented through the potential $u(\lvert x-c\rvert)$ with the same function
$u\in C^2(J_0)$. This model is the **fixed-centre idealization** of the
reduced problem: it drops the centre-of-mass degree of freedom and holds the
force centre fixed. It is a separate adopted model class, not a consequence
of class (i), and every use of it must state that the idealization is
intended.

**(iv) Reading conventions.** In the statements of this page: the **force
centre** of the reduced problem is the origin of the relative coordinate
$r$; an **orbit** is the trajectory $t\mapsto r(t)$ of the reduced problem
(equivalently, by [[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]], the trajectory of either
label relative to the centre of mass, up to the mass ratio); "circular" and
"elliptic" name properties of that trajectory; and the words "planet",
"satellite", "central body" and "test particle" name labels of a model of
class (i) or (iii). These words carry no empirical claim about nature.

**(v) Exclusions and status.** The class excludes: velocity-dependent and
explicitly time-dependent central forces; non-central and non-potential
forces; constraints and reaction forces; colliding configurations
$x_1=x_2$ (equivalently $r=0$); external forces on the labels; and models
with more than two labels. Finite-size, rotational, deformational, dissipative
and relativistic effects are outside the class. The masses, the interval
$J_0$ and the function $u$ (including any parameters it carries) are model
data, not measured values ([[def-cm01-units]]); quantitative empirical use
requires separately stated measured inputs with their uncertainties, and no
statement of this page asserts that any physical system is exactly a model
of this class.
items.strategy: An adopted model class: the two-label static central pair-potential models without external forces, the reduced one-label problem, the fixed-centre idealization, the reading conventions for force centre and orbit, and the exclusions and status of the model data.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the page's central-force model class inside the framework's force and interaction branches: two-label models presented by a static $C^2$ central pair potential on a collision-excluded annulus and free of external forces; the reduced one-label problem of mass $\mu$; the separate one-label fixed-centre idealization; the reading conventions for force centre, orbit and body labels; and the explicit exclusions (velocity- or time-dependent, non-central, non-potential, constrained, colliding, external-force and many-body models) together with the status of the model data. The item adopts a modelling class; it asserts no law of nature, no measured value and no conservation law.

items.title: Planarity of the reduced orbit and the area law: the areal-velocity vector is the constant $j/(2\mu)$, the swept-area rate is $J/(2\mu)$, and both labels sweep equal areas in equal times about the centre of mass
items.statement:
Adopt the central-force model of [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (i): masses
$m_1,m_2>0$, $M=m_1+m_2$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/M$, static central pair
potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$, and a motion $x:I\to Q$ on a time interval $I$ with
nonempty interior; let $X$ be its centre of mass, $r=x_1-x_2$ its relative
coordinate, and $j:=\mu\,r\times r'$ the attached angular-momentum vector
([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]], [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]]). Then:

1. **(Plane.)** $j$ is constant on $I$, and $\langle r(t),j\rangle=0$ and
   $\langle r'(t),j\rangle=0$ for every $t\in I$; if $j\ne0$, the relative
   trajectory is contained in the fixed plane
   $\{y\in\mathbb R^3:\langle y,j\rangle=0\}$ through the force centre with
   normal $j$.
2. **(Areal velocity.)** Suppose $j\ne0$ and write $J:=\lvert j\rvert>0$.
   Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data for $r$ in an oriented orthonormal triad
   with $e_3=j/J$ ([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]). Then
   $\rho^2\theta'=J/\mu>0$, and the **areal-velocity vector**
   $$\omega(t):=\tfrac12\,r(t)\times r'(t)$$
   is constant and equal to $j/(2\mu)$; in particular
   $\lvert\omega(t)\rvert=J/(2\mu)$ for all $t$.
3. **(Equal areas in equal times.)** With $(\rho,\theta)$ as in clause 2 and
   $t_0\in I$, the **swept-area function**
   $$A(t):=\frac12\int_{t_0}^{t}\rho(s)^2\theta'(s)\,ds\qquad(t\in I)$$
   is of class $C^1$ with $A'\equiv J/(2\mu)$; hence for all
   $t_0<t_1$ in $I$ one has $A(t_1)-A(t_0)=(t_1-t_0)J/(2\mu)$.
4. **(Both labels about the centre of mass.)** With $j\ne0$ as in clause 2,
   for every $t\in I$,
   $$\tfrac12\bigl(x_1(t)-X(t)\bigr)\times\bigl(x_1(t)-X(t)\bigr)'=\Bigl(\frac{m_2}{M}\Bigr)^{2}\omega(t),\qquad \tfrac12\bigl(x_2(t)-X(t)\bigr)\times\bigl(x_2(t)-X(t)\bigr)'=\Bigl(\frac{m_1}{M}\Bigr)^{2}\omega(t),$$
   so each label's areal-velocity vector about the centre of mass is
   constant; their magnitudes are in the ratio $(m_2/m_1)^2$.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction from the reduction and the mathematical central-force theorems: constancy and orthogonality of the angular momentum, the constant areal-velocity vector, the linear swept-area function, and the barycentric areal rates of both labels.
items.physical_scope: The planar character of the reduced two-body orbit and the areal law, conditional on the adopted central-force model class: the attached angular-momentum vector is constant and orthogonal to the trajectory; for non-zero angular momentum the areal-velocity vector equals the constant $j/(2\mu)$ and the swept-area function grows linearly; and each label sweeps a constant areal rate about the centre of mass with the mass-ratio factor $(m_2/m_1)^2$. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted model; it reports no observation, no measured value and no conservation beyond the conserved angular momentum of the central model.

items.title: Reduction of the central problem to the effective one-dimensional potential: $\mu\rho''=-(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J)'(\rho)$, the energy identity, and the converse reconstruction of the planar trajectory from the radial data
items.statement:
Adopt the central-force model of [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (i) with
masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/M$, $M=m_1+m_2$, static central
pair potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$, and let $x:I\to Q$ be a motion on a time
interval $I$ with relative
coordinate $r$, attached angular momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'$, and suppose
$j=Je_3$ with $J>0$ for an oriented orthonormal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]], [[lem-cm-oriented-orthonormal-triads]]).
Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data for $r$ in that triad
([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]) and put
$$U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho):=u(\rho)+\frac{J^2}{2\mu\rho^2}\qquad(\rho\in J_0),$$
the **effective potential** of angular momentum $J$, of class $C^2$ on $J_0$
([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]]). Then:

1. **(Radial problem.)** On $I$: $\rho^2\theta'=J/\mu>0$, the effective
   equation
   $$\mu\,\rho''=-\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)'(\rho)$$
   holds, and the relative energy
   $E=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+u(\lvert r\rvert)$ satisfies
   $E=\tfrac12\mu(\rho')^2+U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho)$ and is constant on $I$;
   equivalently, the radial coordinate solves the one-dimensional mechanical
   initial-value problem of mass $\mu$ on the declared radial interval $J_0$
   (an interval contained in $\rho>0$) in the
   potential $U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J$.
2. **(Reconstruction.)** Conversely, let $\rho^{\circ}:I\to\mathbb R$ be a
   $C^2$ function with $\rho^{\circ}(t)\in J_0$ and
   $\mu(\rho^{\circ})''=-(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J)'(\rho^{\circ})$ on $I$, and let
   $\theta^{\circ}:I\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^2$ function with
   $(\theta^{\circ})'=J/\bigl(\mu(\rho^{\circ})^2\bigr)$ on $I$ (for instance
   $\theta^{\circ}(t)=\theta_0+\frac{J}{\mu}\int_{t_0}^{t}\rho^{\circ}(s)^{-2}\mathrm ds$).
   Then
   $$r^{\circ}(t):=\rho^{\circ}(t)\bigl(\cos\theta^{\circ}(t)\,e_1+\sin\theta^{\circ}(t)\,e_2\bigr)\qquad(t\in I)$$
   is a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ with
   $j^{\circ}=\mu\,r^{\circ}\times(r^{\circ})'=Je_3$ and constant energy
   $\tfrac12\mu\bigl((\rho^{\circ})'\bigr)^2+U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho^{\circ})$.
3. **(Mutual inversion and model reconstruction.)** The assignments of
   clauses 1 and 2 are mutually inverse: reconstructing from the polar data
   of $r$ returns $r$, and the polar data of the reconstructed $r^{\circ}$
   agree with $(\rho^{\circ},\theta^{\circ})$ up to an additive constant of
   the angular coordinate. Consequently, together with an affine
   centre-of-mass curve $X^{\circ}$ with $(X^{\circ})''=0$ on $I$, the datum
   $(\rho^{\circ},\theta^{\circ})$ reconstructs a motion of the two-label
   model with angular momentum $Je_3$, centre of mass $X^{\circ}$ and relative
   coordinate $r^{\circ}$ ([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 4).
items.strategy: A reduction with converse: apply the mathematical polar reduction for the radial equation and energy, then reconstruct a planar central-force trajectory from any positive radial solution and its angular quadrature, verifying the equations by differentiation.
items.physical_scope: The one-dimensional reduction of the non-radial central problem in the adopted model class for angular-momentum magnitude J>0: the radial coordinate takes values in the declared open radial interval J_0 and obeys the effective-potential equation with the centrifugal term, its energy is the constant first integral of that one-dimensional problem, and conversely every C^2 radial solution valued in J_0 together with the angular quadrature reconstructs a planar central-force trajectory with the prescribed angular momentum, hence a motion of the two-label model together with a uniform centre-of-mass motion. The result is a conditional deduction; it asserts no observation, no measured value, and no global existence for either side.

items.title: Circular relative orbits of the central model: the critical-point criterion $u'(r_0)=J^2/(\mu r_0^3)$, uniform rotation of both labels about the centre of mass, and the linearised radial frequency
items.statement:
Adopt the central-force model of [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (i) with
masses $m_1,m_2>0$, $M=m_1+m_2$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/M$, and static
central pair potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$, and time window $I_0$. Fix $J>0$, an oriented orthonormal
triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, and a radius $r_0\in J_0$, and put
$$U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho):=u(\rho)+\frac{J^{2}}{2\mu\rho^{2}},\qquad \omega:=\frac{J}{\mu r_0^{2}}.$$
Then:

1. **(Criterion.)** The following are equivalent:
   $$\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)'(r_0)=0;\qquad u'(r_0)=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu r_0^{3}};\qquad \mu\,r_0\,\omega^{2}=u'(r_0).$$
2. **(Existence and the two labels.)** If the condition of clause 1 holds,
   then for every $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$ the curve
   $$r^{\circ}(t):=r_0\bigl(\cos(\theta_0+\omega t)\,e_1 +\sin(\theta_0+\omega t)\,e_2\bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$
   is a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$,
   with $\lvert r^{\circ}\rvert\equiv r_0$, angular momentum
   $j=\mu\,r^{\circ}\times(r^{\circ})'=Je_3$ and constant energy
   $E=U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(r_0)$; and for every interval $I\subseteq I_0$ with nonempty interior and
   affine centre-of-mass curve $X^{\circ}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ with
   $(X^{\circ})''=0$, the restrictions to $I$ reconstruct a motion of the
   two-label model ([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 4) has both
   labels moving uniformly on circles about the centre of mass:
   $$\lvert x_1(t)-X^{\circ}(t)\rvert=\frac{m_2}{M}r_0,\qquad \lvert x_2(t)-X^{\circ}(t)\rvert=\frac{m_1}{M}r_0,$$
   with angular velocity $\omega$ about $X^{\circ}$.
3. **(Necessity.)** Conversely, if a motion of the model has constant
   separation $\lvert r\rvert\equiv r_0$ on a time interval $I$ with nonempty
   interior and nonzero constant angular momentum $j=Je_3$, then
   $\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)'(r_0)=0$ and its polar angular coordinate
   satisfies $\theta'\equiv\omega$; the relative motion is the uniform
   rotation of clause 2 up to the initial value of $\theta$, and both labels
   move uniformly on the circles of clause 2 about the affine centre of mass.
4. **(Linearised radial frequency.)** If
   $\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)'(r_0)=0$ and
   $\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)''(r_0)>0$, then
   $\omega_{\mathrm{lin}}:=\sqrt{\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)''(r_0)/\mu}>0$,
   and a twice differentiable $\delta:I\to\mathbb R$ on an interval $I$ with
   at least two points solves the linearised radial equation
   $$\mu\,\delta''=-\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)''(r_0)\,\delta \qquad\text{on }I$$
   if and only if $\delta(t)=A\cos\bigl(\omega_{\mathrm{lin}}(t-t_0)\bigr)
   +B\sin\bigl(\omega_{\mathrm{lin}}(t-t_0)\bigr)$ for some $A,B\in\mathbb R$
   and $t_0\in I$. This is a statement about the quadratic radial
   approximation at $r_0$; it does not assert nonlinear stability of the
   circular orbit.

items.physical_scope: Circular relative motion in the adopted central model: the critical-point condition of the effective potential, stated equivalently as the balance $\mu r_0\omega^2=u'(r_0)$ between the central force and the circular motion; the explicit uniform rotation of the relative coordinate and of both labels about the centre of mass; the necessity of the condition for a constant separation; and the frequency of the linearised radial equation at a critical point satisfying the nondegeneracy condition $(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J)''(r_0)>0$. items.title: Adopted two-label gravitational model: the inverse-square pair potential with coupling parameters, the empirical mass identification, and the measured value and uncertainty of the Newtonian constant
items.statement:
Adopt the following gravitational model and empirical premises for the
two-body part of this page, inside the force and interaction branches of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]] and the
central-force class of [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (i).

**(i) The two-label gravitational model.** A model of the gravitational
branch is a model of class (i) of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with
$J_0=(0,\infty)$, $Q=\{x=(x_1,x_2):x_1\ne x_2\}$, masses $m_1,m_2>0$ in the
equation of motion, and the **gravitational pair potential**
$$U(x_1,x_2)=-\frac{G_{\mathrm N}\,m_1^{g}m_2^{g}}{\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert},$$
where $G_{\mathrm N}>0$ is the **Newtonian constant of gravitation**, a
constant of dimension $\ell^{3}\mu^{-1}\tau^{-2}$ read in
$\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and $m_1^{g},m_2^{g}>0$ are the
**gravitational coupling parameters** of the labels, primitive model data
distinct from the inertial masses $m_1,m_2$ ([[post-cm02-interactions]]
clause (v), [[def-cm01-units]]). The corresponding central pair potential of
class (i) is $u(\rho)=-\kappa/\rho$ with
$$\kappa:=G_{\mathrm N}\,m_1^{g}m_2^{g}>0,\qquad\text{dimension } \mu\ell^{3}\tau^{-2};$$
it is of class $C^\infty$ on $(0,\infty)$, the model has no external forces,
and coincident configurations are excluded. The force is attractive, and its
inverse-square form is an **adopted law** of this branch, not a consequence
of the equation of motion.

**(ii) The empirical mass identification.** For the quantitative
applications of this page, adopt in addition the identification
$$m_i^{g}=m_i\qquad(i=1,2)$$
of the gravitational coupling parameters with the inertial masses. This is an
**empirical assumption**, not part of clause (i) and not a consequence of the
equation of motion ([[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (vi)); it is the
content of the weak equivalence principle for these labels, and it is
adopted here only where a statement explicitly says so. When it is adopted,
$\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1m_2$, and every conclusion that uses it inherits its
empirical status; statements that never invoke clause (ii) remain conditional
on clause (i) alone, with $\kappa$ expressed through $m_1^{g},m_2^{g}$.

**(iii) The measured value of the constant.** When a model of this page is
used quantitatively, $G_{\mathrm N}$ may be **assigned** the CODATA 2022
recommended value
$$G_{\mathrm N}=6.674\,30(15)\times10^{-11}\ \mathrm{m^{3}\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}},$$
with standard uncertainty $0.000\,15\times10^{-11}$ in the same unit and
relative standard uncertainty $2.2\times10^{-5}$: a qualified empirical
premise, not a definition and not an exact value. The recommendation is a
least-squares value from 16 measurements whose mutual inconsistency led the
CODATA Task Group to expand its uncertainty by a factor of $3.9$, and the
2022 value agrees with the 2018 value because the input data were unchanged.
Any numerical conclusion that uses this assignment inherits the uncertainty
of $G_{\mathrm N}$ together with the uncertainties and conditions of the
other model data actually used; no such numerical conclusion is drawn by
this postulate itself.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** The force equations in clause (i) define the
formal Newtonian point-particle model. The words **weak-field** and
**non-relativistic** specify when it is intended as an approximation to a
relativistic gravitational description. Let $c:=299792458\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
be the speed of light in vacuum, used here only as an external comparison
constant, not as a parameter in the Newtonian equations. For a configuration
$x=(x_1,x_2)\in Q$ with $\rho(x):=\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert>0$, define the
source potentials per unit gravitational coupling as scalar functions
$\Phi_1,\Phi_2:Q\to\mathbb R$ by
$$\Phi_1(x):=-\frac{G_{\mathrm N}m_2^{g}}{\rho(x)},\qquad \Phi_2(x):=-\frac{G_{\mathrm N}m_1^{g}}{\rho(x)},$$
each of dimension $\ell^2\tau^{-2}$, and for a state velocity
$v=(v_1,v_2)\in(\mathbb R^3)^2$ define the dimensionless parameters
$$\epsilon_{\Phi}(x):=\frac{\max\{\lvert\Phi_1(x)\rvert,\lvert\Phi_2(x)\rvert\}}{c^2},\qquad \epsilon_v(v):=\frac{\lvert v_1-v_2\rvert^2}{c^2}.$$
For a motion $x:J\to Q$, a trajectory interval $\mathcal I\subseteq J$ and a dimensionless tolerance
$\eta\in(0,1)$ chosen small enough for the intended approximation, the
weak-field, slow-relative-motion regime on that segment means
$$\epsilon_{\Phi}(x(t))\le\eta\quad\text{and}\quad\epsilon_v(x'(t))\le\eta\qquad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal I.$$
The choice of $\eta$ is application-specific; this model supplies no
relativistic correction estimate or error bound. When $G_{\mathrm N}$ is
assigned the value in clause (iii), these inequalities inherit its standard
uncertainty and any uncertainty in the other inputs; no regime assessment is
made here. The model treats the two
labels as point particles with fixed masses, ignores external bodies,
rotation, deformation, mass loss, radiation and any non-gravitational force,
and excludes coincident configurations. It is not asserted that any physical
system is exactly of this form; in particular, the identification of clause
(ii) is not a framework-wide identification, and the inverse-square law is
not derived from the balance laws of the framework.

**(v) Status.** Clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) are adopted assumptions of the
model and its empirical inputs; this item contains no proof and no
measurement of its own. The theorems of this page that invoke the model are
conditional on these clauses, and agreement of their predictions with
observations would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions rather
than prove them.
items.strategy: An adopted model and empirical premises: the inverse-square pair potential with the Newtonian constant and gravitational couplings, the empirical identification with the inertial masses, the measured value of the constant with its uncertainty and the inconsistency of its measurements, and the non-relativistic weak-field scope.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the two-label gravitational model inside the page's central-force class: the inverse-square static pair potential with the Newtonian constant and positive gravitational coupling parameters; the empirical identification of the coupling parameters with the inertial masses, adopted as an assumption of the page's applications; the measured value of the Newtonian constant with its uncertainty and the mutual inconsistency of its measurements; and the non-relativistic weak-field two-point-label applicability regime, specified by the source-potential and relative-speed inequalities in clause (iv), with its exclusions. The item adopts model data and empirical premises; it asserts no law of nature, no proof of the identification, and no numerical prediction by itself.

items.title: The inverse-square gravitational relative trajectory has the Kepler polar form: $\rho=p/(1+e\cos(\theta-\theta_0))$, $E=(\mu\kappa^2/2J^2)(e^2-1)$, elliptic completeness and barycentric scaled ellipses
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the
two-label gravitational model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (i): inertial
masses $m_1,m_2>0$, $M=m_1+m_2$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/M$, gravitational
couplings $m_1^{g},m_2^{g}>0$, $\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1^{g}m_2^{g}>0$, and
the central pair potential $u(\rho)=-\kappa/\rho$ on $J_0=(0,\infty)$,
and model time window $I_0$. Let
$x:I\to Q$ be a motion on a time interval $I$ with nonempty interior, with
relative coordinate $r$, attached angular momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'$ and
energy $E=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2-\kappa/\lvert r\rvert$
([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]], [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]]), and
suppose $j=Je_3$, $J>0$, for an oriented orthonormal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$.
Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data for $r$ and put
$$p:=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa},\qquad U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho):=-\frac{\kappa}{\rho}+\frac{J^{2}}{2\mu\rho^{2}},\qquad \rho_*:=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa}=p.$$
Then:

In the orbital plane $\Pi:=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2)$, for a point
$F\in\Pi$, a line $D\subseteq\Pi$ with $F\notin D$, and $e>0$, define the
**focus-directrix conic of eccentricity $e$** to be
$$C(F,D,e):=\{y\in\Pi:\lVert y-F\rVert_2=e\,d_\Pi(y,D)\},\qquad d_\Pi(y,D):=\inf_{z\in D}\lVert y-z\rVert_2.$$
Here $F$ is a focus, $D$ is its directrix, and $e$ is the distance ratio in
the definition. The types $0<e<1$, $e=1$, and $e>1$ are called ellipse,
parabola, and hyperbola, respectively. The case $e=0$ is the circle of radius
$p$ centered at $F$, the circular ellipse with coincident foci at its centre.
In this item, an **unbounded conic** is a conic locus that is unbounded, not
an open subset of $\Pi$; the **periapsis distance** is the minimum distance
on the conic to its focus, and any point attaining it is a periapsis.

1. **(Conic and eccentricity.)** There are $e\ge0$ and $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$
   with
   $$\rho=\frac{p}{1+e\cos(\theta-\theta_0)}$$
   on the interior of $I$, and the energy satisfies
   $E=\dfrac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2J^{2}}\bigl(e^{2}-1\bigr)$; consequently
   $E<0\iff e<1$, $E=0\iff e=1$ and $E>0\iff e>1$. The relative trajectory
   lies on a focus-directrix conic with the force centre as focus when $e>0$: its
   directrix is $D=\{y\in\Pi:\langle y,n_0\rangle=p/e\}$, where
   $n_0:=\cos\theta_0e_1+\sin\theta_0e_2$. When $e=0$, the relative
   trajectory lies on the circle of radius $p$ centered at the force centre.
2. **(Centrifugal barrier.)** $\rho_*$ is the unique critical point of
   $U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J$ in $(0,\infty)$ and the unique minimum, with
   $$U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho_*)=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2J^{2}};$$
   setting
   $$\rho_{\min}(E):=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa+\sqrt{\mu^{2}\kappa^{2}+2\mu EJ^{2}}}>0,$$
   one has $U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho_{\min}(E))=E$ and
   $\rho(t)\ge\rho_{\min}(E)$ for every $t\in I$. In particular the relative
   motion never reaches the collision $r=0$, and
   $\rho_{\min}(E)=p/(1+e)$ is the periapsis distance of the conic of
   clause 1.
3. **(Elliptic case.)** If $E<0$, then $e<1$ and:
   (a) the relative trajectory extends uniquely to a central-force
   trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$. Together with
   the unique affine extension of $X$, this defines global coordinate curves
   $\bar x_1=\bar X+(m_2/M)\bar r$, $\bar x_2=\bar X-(m_1/M)\bar r$
   satisfying the same time-independent force equations; their restriction
   to $I_0$ is the unique extension of the model motion $x$. They are a
   model motion on all of $\mathbb R$ when $I_0=\mathbb R$. The relative
   motion is periodic, with
   $\theta(t+T)=\theta(t)+2\pi$ for one full angular revolution;
   (b) $r$ is an ellipse with focus at the force centre, semiaxes
   $$a=\frac{p}{1-e^{2}}=-\frac{\kappa}{2E},\qquad b=a\sqrt{1-e^{2}},$$
   and $p/(1+e)\le\rho\le p/(1-e)$;
   (c) each label's trajectory relative to the centre of mass is the conic
   of clause 1 scaled by $m_j/M$: with
   $p_1:=\frac{m_2}{M}p$, $p_2:=\frac{m_1}{M}p$ one has
   $$\lvert x_1-X\rvert=\frac{p_1}{1+e\cos(\theta-\theta_0)},\qquad \lvert x_2-X\rvert=\frac{p_2}{1+e\cos(\theta-\theta_0)},$$
   so both labels trace ellipses with the centre of mass at a focus, the
   same eccentricity $e$ and semimajor axes $a_1=\frac{m_2}{M}a$,
   $a_2=\frac{m_1}{M}a$.
4. **(Parabolic and hyperbolic cases on the domain of the motion.)** If
   $E=0$, then $e=1$ and
   $\rho=p/\bigl(1+\cos(\theta-\theta_0)\bigr)$ with periapsis
   $\rho_{\min}(0)=p/2$. If $E>0$, then $e>1$ and the formula of clause 1
   holds at every $t$ with $1+e\cos(\theta-\theta_0)>0$, with periapsis
   $\rho_{\min}(E)=p/(1+e)$. In both cases $e\ge1$ and the corresponding
   conic locus is unbounded;
   the extent of the trajectory, its asymptotes and its scattering
   interpretation are **not** claimed here.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: apply the mathematical Binet and conic theorems to the gravitational relative trajectory, prove the centrifugal-barrier bound by monotonicity of the effective potential, and instantiate completeness, ellipse geometry and the barycentric scaled conics; the open branches are recorded without extent claims.
items.physical_scope: The Keplerian orbit classification of the two-label gravitational model with non-zero angular momentum: the polar conic with its eccentricity and focus at the force centre, the eccentricity-energy relation and the elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic branches, the centrifugal barrier that keeps the motion away from the collision, and - in the elliptic case - the completeness of the relative trajectory and reconstruction on the declared model time window, the closed periodic relative orbit with the ellipse geometry, and the scaled barycentric conics of both labels. The parabolic and hyperbolic clauses record only the orbit formula, the periapsis and the domain of the angle on the actual domain of the motion; no asymptotic extent, scattering or observational claim is made.

items.title: Kepler's third law for the gravitational two-label model: the relative period is $T=2\pi\mu ab/J=2\pi\sqrt{\mu/\kappa}\,a^{3/2}$, so $T^2=4\pi^2a^3/(G_{\mathrm N}M)$ under the mass identification, and both labels are periodic relative to the centre of mass
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the
two-label gravitational model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (i): inertial
masses $m_1,m_2>0$, $M=m_1+m_2$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/M$, gravitational
couplings $m_1^{g},m_2^{g}>0$, $\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1^{g}m_2^{g}$, and the
potential $u(\rho)=-\kappa/\rho$ on $(0,\infty)$. Let $x:I\to Q$ be a motion
on a time interval $I$ with relative coordinate $r$, angular momentum
$j=Je_3$, $J>0$, and energy
$E<0$, and let $e\in[0,1)$, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$,
$$p=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa},\qquad a=\frac{p}{1-e^{2}}=-\frac{\kappa}{2E},\qquad b=a\sqrt{1-e^{2}}$$
be its conic data ([[pthm-cm05-conic]] clauses 1 and 3). Then:

1. **(Period of the relative motion.)** The relative motion extends uniquely
   to a central-force trajectory on all of $\mathbb R$ (as in
   [[pthm-cm05-conic]] clause 3); along that extension (with $\theta$ its
   polar angular coordinate, as supplied by the cited orbit theory), if
   $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and $T>0$ is determined by
   $\theta(t_0+T)=\theta(t_0)+2\pi$, then $r(t+T)=r(t)$ and
   $r'(t+T)=r'(t)$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, and
   $$T=\frac{2\pi\mu ab}{J}=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\kappa}}\,a^{3/2}, \qquad T^{2}=\frac{4\pi^{2}\mu a^{3}}{\kappa}.$$
2. **(Gravitational parameters.)** With $\mu=m_1m_2/M$ and
   $\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1^{g}m_2^{g}$,
   $$T^{2}=\frac{4\pi^{2}a^{3}m_1m_2}{M\,G_{\mathrm N}\,m_1^{g}m_2^{g}};$$
   if in addition the model adopts the identification
   $m_i^{g}=m_i$ of [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (ii), this reduces to
   $$T^{2}=\frac{4\pi^{2}a^{3}}{G_{\mathrm N}M}.$$
3. **(Both labels.)** On the global coordinate extension supplied by
   [[pthm-cm05-conic]] clause 3(a) (write it again as $x$, with centre
   of mass $X$), for each $i=1,2$ the position relative to
   the centre of mass is periodic with period $T$,
   $x_i(t+T)-X(t+T)=x_i(t)-X(t)$, while the absolute motions satisfy
   $$x_i(t+T)-x_i(t)=V\,T\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
   with the constant centre-of-mass velocity $V=X'$ of
   [[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 2; the absolute motions are
   periodic exactly when $V=0$. The restriction of this extension to the
   model time window $I_0$ is a model motion; statements about
   $x_i(t+T)$ within that model require $t,t+T\in I_0$.
4. **(Area per period.)** The area swept by the relative radius vector in one
   period is $\pi ab$, and it equals $JT/(2\mu)$; equivalently
   $T=2\pi\mu ab/J$ as in clause 1.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: instantiate the mathematical completeness and period theorems for the negative-energy Kepler orbit, substitute the gravitational parameters including the mass identification, derive the periodicity of both labels from the affine centre of mass, and identify the area swept per period with the ellipse area.
items.physical_scope: The period of the negative-energy gravitational relative orbit in the adopted two-label model: the relative motion is periodic, its period is $2\pi\mu ab/J=2\pi\sqrt{\mu/\kappa}\,a^{3/2}$, the form $T^2=4\pi^2a^3/(G_{\mathrm N}M)$ holds when the gravitational couplings are identified with the inertial masses, each label is periodic about the centre of mass while its absolute motion advances by $VT$ per period, and the area swept per period is $\pi ab$. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted model and its declared empirical identification; it reports no observation and no measured value.

items.title: Scope of the two-body and central-force page: collision and radial exclusions, point-particle and finite-size limits, the empirical parameters and their uncertainty, and the conditional status of the orbit statements
items.statement:
## Status audit of this page

This remark records the scope of the page's items. It is bookkeeping: every
mathematical statement it repeats is proved in the item cited, and it adds no
law, no observation and no numerical value of its own.

**Adopted assumptions.** The force branch is [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]
with its standing regularity and equation of motion; the interaction
restrictions (external-plus-pair presentation, antisymmetry, centrality, the
potential branch and the gravitational branch) are [[post-cm02-interactions]];
the page's central-force class, the reduced problem, the fixed-centre
idealization and the reading conventions are [[post-cm05-central-model]]; and
the gravitational model with its mass identification and the measured value
of $G_{\mathrm N}$ is [[post-cm05-gravity]]. None of these is proved here.

**Conditional deductions.** The relative reduction, the uniform
centre-of-mass motion and the reconstruction bijection are
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]]; the planarity and area law are
[[pthm-cm05-plane-area]]; the effective one-dimensional problem and its
converse are [[pthm-cm05-effective-potential]]; the circular-orbit criterion
and the linearised radial frequency are [[pthm-cm05-circular-orbit]]; the
conic classification, the barrier and the elliptic geometry are
[[pthm-cm05-conic]]; and the period and third law are
[[pthm-cm05-kepler-period]]. Each is a conditional consequence of the adopted
model and the cited mathematics. The conic and period items assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); every scope statement below
that invokes their conclusions carries that assumption.

## Exclusions and limits

- **Collision and the domain.** The configuration domain excludes
  $x_1=x_2$, i.e. $r=0$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]],
  [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (v)); the equations of motion and every
  orbit statement above are undefined at the collision. In the gravitational
  model with $j\ne0$ the barrier of [[pthm-cm05-conic]] clause 2 keeps
  $\lvert r\rvert\ge\rho_{\min}(E)>0$ throughout the motion; no such bound is
  available for the radial case, so the conic, area and period statements
  must not be extended to it.

- **Radial motion.** For $j=0$ no polar angle and no plane orthogonal to a
  nonzero $j$ exist; [[pthm-cm05-plane-area]] clauses 2-4,
  [[pthm-cm05-conic]] and [[pthm-cm05-kepler-period]] exclude this case
  explicitly, and [[pthm-cm05-effective-potential]] clause 1 then reduces to
  the one-dimensional equation of the sign-constant direction. No
  equal-area, conic or period claim is made for radial trajectories.

- **Point particles and finite size.** The model retains only positions and
  fixed masses of the labels ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (vi)); size,
  shape, rotation, deformation, internal structure and mass loss are omitted.
  A real body whose radius, multipole moments, tides or spin matter for the
  question asked is not described by these items, and their applicability
  must be justified separately wherever they are used.

- **External bodies and non-gravitational forces.** The model has no
  external forces by construction ([[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (i)),
  so third bodies, drag, radiation pressure or any other agent are outside
  it; a two-body computation with such influences is a different model,
  not a corollary of this page.

- **Regime.** The model is non-relativistic and weak-field; relativistic
  corrections (for instance the perihelion precession of the inner planets)
  require the general-relativistic framework and are not derived or bounded
  here. The inverse-square law itself is an adopted law of the model.

## Empirical status

- **The constant.** Formula-level statements use the symbol $G_{\mathrm N}$
  and are conditional on [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (i). Any numerical
  application that assigns the CODATA value of clause (iii) — relative
  standard uncertainty $2.2\times10^{-5}$, with the mutual inconsistency of
  the 16 input measurements recorded there — inherits that uncertainty and
  the conditions of every other input actually used. The framework does not
  derive the value of $G_{\mathrm N}$ and does not claim it is exact.

- **The mass identification.** The simplification of the third law to
  $T^{2}=4\pi^{2}a^{3}/(G_{\mathrm N}M)$ in [[pthm-cm05-kepler-period]] clause
  2 uses the empirical identification $m_i^{g}=m_i$ of
  [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (ii), which is an adopted assumption, not a
  consequence of the equation of motion. Statements that keep the couplings
  $m_i^{g}$ distinct remain valid without it.

- **No observations.** No item of this page reports an experiment,
  calibration, count or uncertainty of a measurement; the numerical checks
  collected on the companion examples page use declared model data. Comparing
  any prediction of this page with observations would test the combined
  model, parameter and apparatus assumptions; agreement would be evidence,
  not a proof of the model, and a discrepancy would identify no particular
  postulate by itself.

## Deliberately not claimed

No global existence of arbitrary central-force trajectories, no nonlinear
stability of circular orbits, no closed-form solution of the general
non-Coulomb central problem, no asymptotes or scattering cross-sections for
the open branches, no relativistic or finite-size corrections, and no claim
that any physical system is exactly a model of the adopted class.

items.title: An elliptic gravitational relative orbit checked on declared model data: $p=10^{6}\,$m, $e=3/5$, $a=25\cdot10^{6}/16\,$m, $b=5\cdot10^{6}/4\,$m, $E=-3.2\cdot10^{17}\,$J and $T=125\pi\cdot10^{9}/32\,$s, with $T^{2}=4\pi^{2}a^{3}/(G_{\mathrm N}M)$
items.statement:
Declare the gravitational two-label model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (i)
with time window $I_0=\mathbb R$ and the following **model data** (decimal numbers declared for this
computation; $G_{\mathrm N}=2.5\times10^{-25}\ \mathrm{m^{3}\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$
is a declared datum of the example, **not** the measured value of clause
(iii), and the couplings are identified with the inertial masses as in clause
(ii)):
$$m_1=m_2=2\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad M=4\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad \mu=\frac{m_1m_2}{M}=10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad \kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1m_2=10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}.$$
Suppose a motion $x$ of this model has a relative orbit with angular momentum
magnitude $J=10^{27}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}$, conic parameter
$$p=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa}=10^{6}\ \mathrm{m},$$
and eccentricity $e=\tfrac35$ (the conic data of
[[pthm-cm05-conic]] clause 1). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]), as in the cited conic and period items. Then the
cited items predict, as exact consequences of these data:

1. the energy $E=\dfrac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2J^{2}}\bigl(e^{2}-1\bigr)=-\dfrac{8}{25}\times10^{18}\ \mathrm J=-3.2\times10^{17}\ \mathrm J$, and $E<0$ with $e<1$, consistent with the elliptic branch;
2. the semiaxes $a=\dfrac{p}{1-e^{2}}=\dfrac{25}{16}\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$ and $b=a\sqrt{1-e^{2}}=\dfrac54\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$, with $a=-\kappa/(2E)$;
3. the relative period $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu a^{3}}{\kappa}}=2\pi\dfrac{\mu ab}{J}=\dfrac{125\pi}{32}\times10^{9}\ \mathrm s$, so $T^{2}=\dfrac{4\pi^{2}\mu a^{3}}{\kappa}$;
4. the third-law form $T^{2}=\dfrac{4\pi^{2}a^{3}}{G_{\mathrm N}M}$ of [[pthm-cm05-kepler-period]] clause 2 under the declared identification;
5. the areal rate $J/(2\mu)=500\ \mathrm{m^{2}\,s^{-1}}$ and the identity $\pi ab/T=J/(2\mu)$;
6. both labels trace ellipses with the centre of mass at a focus, the same eccentricity $e$, and semimajor axes $a_1=a_2=\tfrac12a=\dfrac{25}{32}\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$ (equal masses), each periodic about the centre of mass with period $T$.
items.strategy: A worked verification: declare the gravitational data, substitute the conic parameter and eccentricity into the cited formulas, and check the energy, semiaxes, two period routes, the third-law form, the areal rate and the barycentric semiaxes by exact arithmetic.

items.title: The parabolic and hyperbolic branches on declared model data: $E=0$ with $e=1$ and periapsis $p/2$, and $E=1.5\cdot10^{18}\,$J with $e=2$, periapsis $p/3$ and angular domain $\lvert\theta-\theta_0\rvert<2\pi/3$
items.statement:
Declare the same model data as the companion elliptic check
([[ex-cm05-gravitational-ellipse-and-period-check]]): the gravitational
two-label model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] with
$$m_1=m_2=2\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\quad \mu=10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\quad \kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1m_2=10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}},\quad J=10^{27}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}},\quad p=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa}=10^{6}\ \mathrm m,$$
where $G_{\mathrm N}=2.5\times10^{-25}\ \mathrm{m^{3}\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ is a
declared datum of the computation and the couplings are identified with the
inertial masses. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]), as in the cited conic item. On this data the
formulas of [[pthm-cm05-conic]] give:

1. **Parabolic branch.** The energy $E=0$ corresponds to eccentricity
   $e=1$; the conic is $\rho=p/\bigl(1+\cos(\theta-\theta_0)\bigr)$, whose
   denominator ranges over $(0,2]$, and the periapsis is
   $\rho_{\min}(0)=p/2=5\times10^{5}\ \mathrm m$, with
   $U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(\rho_{\min}(0))=0=E$.
2. **Hyperbolic branch.** With eccentricity $e=2$ the energy is
   $$E=\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2J^{2}}\bigl(e^{2}-1\bigr)=\tfrac32\times10^{18}\ \mathrm J,$$
   the periapsis is $\rho_{\min}(E)=p/(1+e)=10^{6}/3\ \mathrm m$, with
   $U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigl(10^{6}/3\bigr)=E$, and the orbit is the branch
   $$\rho=\frac{p}{1+2\cos(\theta-\theta_0)}$$
   evaluated where $1+2\cos(\theta-\theta_0)>0$, that is
   $\lvert\theta-\theta_0\rvert<2\pi/3$ modulo $2\pi$.
3. **Consistency of the classification.** In both cases $e\ge1$ and the
   corresponding focus-directrix conic loci of [[pthm-cm05-conic]] are
   unbounded; the barrier of clause 2 gives
   $\rho\ge\rho_{\min}(E)>0$ along the motion, so the collision is excluded;
   no claim is made that the motion traverses the entire locus.
items.strategy: A worked verification: on declared data with eccentricities one and two, check the zero- and positive-energy correspondences, the periapsis distances as zeros of the effective potential, the hyperbolic angular domain and the barrier bound.
items.physical_scope: A numerical consistency check of the zero- and positive-energy branches of the gravitational relative orbit on declared model data: the eccentricity-energy correspondence $E=0\iff e=1$ and $E>0\iff e>1$, the periapsis distances as zeros of the effective potential, the angular domain of the hyperbolic branch and the barrier bound. items.title: Barycentric orbits of two unequal masses on declared model data: $p_1=(m_2/M)p$, $p_2=(m_1/M)p$, semiaxes in the ratio $3:1$ and areal rates in the ratio $9:1$
items.statement:
Declare the gravitational two-label model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] with
time window $I_0=\mathbb R$, unequal inertial masses and a declared value of the constant,
$$m_1=2\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\quad m_2=6\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\quad M=8\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\quad \mu=\frac{m_1m_2}{M}=\tfrac32\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},$$
$$G_{\mathrm N}=10^{-24}\ \mathrm{m^{3}\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}},\qquad \kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1m_2=1.2\times10^{25}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}},$$
with the couplings identified with the inertial masses, and suppose a motion
has relative conic data
$$J=6\times10^{27}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}},\qquad p=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa}=2\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m,\qquad e=\tfrac12.$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as in the
cited conic and period items. Then the cited items give:

1. the relative semiaxes $a=p/(1-e^{2})=\tfrac83\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$ and
   $b=a\sqrt{1-e^{2}}=\tfrac{4\sqrt3}{3}\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$, energy
   $E=-\kappa/(2a)=-\tfrac94\times10^{18}\ \mathrm J$, and period
   $T=2\pi\sqrt{\mu a^{3}/\kappa}=\tfrac{16\pi}{3\sqrt3}\times10^{9}\ \mathrm s$;
2. each label's orbit about the centre of mass is the scaled ellipse with
   parameters
   $$p_1=\frac{m_2}{M}p=\tfrac32\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m,\qquad p_2=\frac{m_1}{M}p=\tfrac12\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m,$$
   the same eccentricity $e=\tfrac12$, focus at the centre of mass and
   semimajor axes $a_1=\tfrac34a=2\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$,
   $a_2=\tfrac14a=\tfrac23\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$;
3. the areal-velocity magnitudes about the centre of mass are in the ratio
   $(m_2/m_1)^{2}=9$:
   $$\Bigl(\frac{m_2}{M}\Bigr)^{2}\frac{J}{2\mu}=1125\ \mathrm{m^{2}\,s^{-1}},\qquad \Bigl(\frac{m_1}{M}\Bigr)^{2}\frac{J}{2\mu}=125\ \mathrm{m^{2}\,s^{-1}};$$
4. both labels are periodic about the centre of mass with the common period
   $T$.
items.strategy: A worked verification with unequal masses: check the scaled conic parameters and semiaxes of both labels about the centre of mass, the common eccentricity and focus, the areal rates in the mass-ratio-squared ratio and the common period.
items.physical_scope: A numerical check of the barycentric reconstruction on declared model data with unequal masses: the two labels' conic parameters and semimajor axes, the common eccentricity and focus at the centre of mass, the ratio of the areal rates $(m_2/m_1)^2$ and the common period about the centre of mass. items.title: A gravitational circular relative orbit checked on declared model data: $r_0=2\cdot10^{6}\,$m, $\mu r_0\omega^2=u'(r_0)=3\cdot10^{12}\,$N, $E=-3\cdot10^{18}\,$J and $\omega_{\rm lin}=\omega=10^{-9}\,$s$^{-1}$
items.statement:
Declare the gravitational two-label model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] with
time window $I_0=\mathbb R$ and the
same data as the barycentric check ([[ex-cm05-barycentric-orbits-check]]):
$$m_1=2\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad m_2=6\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad \mu=\tfrac32\times10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad G_{\mathrm N}=10^{-24}\ \mathrm{m^{3}\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}},$$
$$\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1m_2=1.2\times10^{25}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}},\qquad J=6\times10^{27}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}},$$
with the couplings identified with the inertial masses. Then
[[pthm-cm05-circular-orbit]] gives:

1. the critical radius and angular velocity
   $$r_0=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa}=2\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m,\qquad \omega=\frac{J}{\mu r_0^{2}}=10^{-9}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}},$$
   and the criterion holds in all three equivalent forms
   $\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)'(r_0)=0$,
   $u'(r_0)=J^{2}/(\mu r_0^{3})=3\times10^{12}\ \mathrm N$,
   $\mu r_0\omega^{2}=3\times10^{12}\ \mathrm N$;
2. the orbital energy $E=U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J(r_0)=-\mu\kappa^{2}/(2J^{2})=-3\times10^{18}\ \mathrm J$, the minimum of the effective potential;
3. the linearised radial frequency
   $\omega_{\mathrm{lin}}=\sqrt{\bigl(U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J\bigr)''(r_0)/\mu}=\sqrt{\kappa/(\mu r_0^{3})}=10^{-9}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$,
   equal to the orbital angular velocity $\omega$ for this inverse-square
   potential;
4. both labels move uniformly on circles about the centre of mass with
   angular velocity $\omega=10^{-9}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and radii
   $\frac{m_2}{M}r_0=1.5\times10^{6}\ \mathrm m$ and
   $\frac{m_1}{M}r_0=5\times10^{5}\ \mathrm m$, each with period
   $2\pi/\omega=2\pi\times10^{9}\ \mathrm s$.

The stated period is relative to the centre of mass, for the coordinates
$x_i-X$. An absolute label trajectory has this period only if the centre of
mass velocity $V$ vanishes; otherwise the centre of mass drifts uniformly.
items.strategy: A worked verification: compute the critical radius and angular velocity on declared data, check the three equivalent forms of the circular criterion, the energy at the minimum of the effective potential, the equality of the linearised radial and orbital frequencies and the labels' circles.
items.physical_scope: A numerical check of the circular-orbit criterion and the linearised radial frequency on declared model data for the gravitational relative problem: the critical radius, the force-balance identity $\mu r_0\omega^2=u'(r_0)$, the energy at the minimum of the effective potential, the equality $\omega_{\rm lin}=\omega$ for the inverse-square potential, and the two labels' circular motions about the centre of mass. items.title: External forces break the two-body reduction: a two-label model with a static central pair potential and external forces $\pm\gamma$ has $\mu r''=\gamma\ne0$, although its total external force vanishes
items.statement:
**False statement.** *Let a two-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] declare the external-plus-pair presentation
of [[post-cm02-interactions]] with a static central pair potential
$u\in C^2(J_0)$, with **no** restriction on the external forces. Then the
relative coordinate $r=x_1-x_2$ of every motion is a central-force trajectory
for $(\mu,u)$ with $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, that is
$\mu r''=-u'(\lvert r\rvert)r/\lvert r\rvert$.*

The hypothesis of [[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] is the stronger statement
that the force map be presented through the potential
$U(x)=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert)$ alone, which excludes external forces; the
witness below shows that this exclusion is not decorative. In particular the
vanishing of the total external force, which already guarantees the
centre-of-mass balance of [[pthm-cm03-momentum-balance]], is not sufficient
for the reduction.
items.strategy: A direct refutation: derive the relative-acceleration identity with external forces, exhibit a model with zero pair potential and antisymmetric constant external forces and an explicit motion, and show that the reduced central-force equation fails although the total external force vanishes.
items.physical_scope: A refutation of the unconditional two-body reduction: an explicit two-label force model with the external-plus-pair presentation, a (zero) static central pair potential and antisymmetric constant external forces has an explicit motion whose relative coordinate is not a central-force trajectory, even though the total external force and the centre-of-mass balance are unaffected. The item is a finite check inside the adopted force branch; it asserts no observation and identifies only the necessity of the no-external-force hypothesis of the reduction theorem.
